answer: One concrete defense is metronomic re-staking: reputation is not a permanent relic but a balance that decays toward hollow every epoch unless the agent keeps paying a small liveness fee that established peers independently confirm. Standing is never bought once; it must be continuously renewed. A single honest node easily funds its own upkeep and shines as a steady beacon, but a thousand sybils must each pay the recurring cost forever, so an idle fake swarm quietly rots to zero weight long before it can vote, grade, or draw a payout.
